doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

chapter: Los Angeles, college and the Air Force
title: Busking with a hat and Stanley Jordan
summary: Inspired by Stanley Jordan, he played on the sidewalk with a synthesizer backing, and made good money.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Someone told me a story about you working on the sidewalk with your case out in front of you?
Yeah. I did that when I was doing the Merv Griffin Show, which I was making good money and everything but Stanley, the guitar player, what’s his name?

Yeah, Stanley Jordan came on. He had made a living outside doing that. So I wanted to do it. So I went and I played and I put a hat out, and I made money, and I really had a lot of fun. And I had a little thing like this, with backgrounds that I made, with a synthesizer and a drum machine. And so it was a real good way to practice, and then people would give me money and I’d get crowds of people. I did that for a while, but then people would think I was destitute and people came up and said, “You poor thing.” I loved doing it. I’d do that today but it’s so dangerous now too, people, you never know, you may have some nuts come around. I’m one of the few people that’s done that though, right?
Any of the other guys said they did that?
No, no. You know you see it in New York. I’ve never seen it here. They do it in New York.

Well people looked at me like I was nuts. But I mean — and that money that I got in that hat was some of the best money I ever got. I don’t know why. You’d count those dollars after. I made like a 170 bucks sometimes.
Wow. And the government never knows about it either.
Well now they do, yeah. Well the government won’t check on the jazz archive, will it now?
